summary: Researched the evening before (Fri 13 Nov) and re-checked this morning (Sat 14 Nov) with live prices; lineups are not out yet, so the pre-kickoff check re-tests the picks. Saturday of the international break: four Nations League games were researched first and all four are kept at medium; the other candidates (NHL, LoL, WTA Finals, ATP, SHL/KHL/Liiga, UFC 334, other Nations League games, one Brasileirão game) were not researched because the four kept games already make a medium slip. Norway over Wales (p 0.77; no overnight news; Haaland and Odegaard expected; both sides must win, Norway lost 3 of 4 group games and Wales won the last three meetings). Portugal over Denmark (p 0.62; Portugal 4 from 4 but already through, missing Cancelo, Conceicao and Mendes, Ronaldo retired from internationals as reported on 5 Nov; Denmark scored in all four group games). Sweden over Bosnia (p 0.66, up from 0.62: overnight the market moved from 0.633 to 0.683 with DraftKings shortening to 1.40; Bosnia's coach confirmed Muharemovic suspended and Hadzikadunic out, Dzeko has retired; no new Sweden injury; Bosnia unbeaten in the group and drew 1-1 in October). Austria over Ireland (p 0.57, draw 0.265, so only double chance or draw no bet; this morning's Austrian press confirms Xaver Schlager and Prass are out with thigh injuries on top of Wimmer, Alaba and Wanner; no clean sheet in 8; 2-2 in Dublin in October; Elo Austria 1841 v Ireland 1711). Afternoon update (about 16:00 UTC): Norway–Wales was re-checked with the reported XIs (Haaland, Odegaard and goalkeeper Selvik start, no rotation) and stays medium; Norway drifted slightly (DraftKings 1.21 to 1.25). At live prices the best slip is now on the 19:45 games, which get their final check with confirmed lineups at about 18:45 UTC. Final check (about 18:46 UTC, an hour before the 19:45 games): the official XIs for Austria–Ireland and Sweden–Bosnia are out and confirm the morning picture. Sweden field Isak, Gyokeres and Gudmundsson, and Austria start their strongest available side. Neither price has moved against the favourite, so both games are raised to high. For Portugal–Denmark no official XI could be read, and Portugal's price has drifted from 0.645 to 0.605 in 24 hours with no news found, so it stays medium.

checks.team_news: Norway: Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle) and Fredrik Aursnes withdrew on 8 Nov, and Sondre Langas is out with a groin problem. Sorloth was back from a muscle injury per the morning sources, but he is not in the reported XI. Haaland and Odegaard are both in the reported starting XI. Wales: Ben Cabango and Sorba Thomas are suspended, and Kieffer Moore withdrew (Aaron Collins called up). Joe Rodon, Harry Wilson and goalkeeper Karl Darlow are back from injury and are in the reported XI. Several Norway and Wales players are one booking from a ban, Odegaard among them. New today: no further injury, illness or withdrawal news turned up in the web search or on ESPN.
checks.lineups: New today: 101greatgoals (an aggregator, not an official federation or ESPN feed) published both XIs as confirmed, with no clock time. Norway: Selvik; Ryerson, Ajer, Heggem, Moller Wolfe; Berge, Aasgaard, Odegaard; Bobb, Nusa, Haaland. Wales: Darlow; Williams, Rodon, Davies, Dasilva; Ampadu, James, Cullen, Johnson, Wilson, Koumas. The goalkeeper question is settled as Selvik, not Nyland. Haaland and Odegaard start. Norway has Aasgaard in midfield and Heggem at centre-back, in place of the morning prediction's Berg and Ostigard. The Norway XI looks strong with no heavy rotation. The ESPN summary (event 401861165) had no rosters yet, and I found no official federation (fotball.no, FA Wales) post. One non-official source, so not fully confirmed.
checks.rotation: No rotation seen. The reported Norway XI keeps Haaland, Odegaard, Nusa, Bobb, Berge and Selvik, even with the Denmark game on 17 Nov. Wales are also at close to full strength, with Rodon and Wilson back. Unchanged from the morning: both sides need the win.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Group A4 is tight, Norway must beat Wales to keep quarter-final hopes alive, and Wales are level on 3 points and will go all in. Both sides have strong motivation, which keeps draw and upset risk above that of a one-sided fixture.
checks.form: Unchanged from the morning. Norway's last five are L W L L L (7 scored, 10 conceded), with three defeats from four group games. Wales' last five are L L L W L (3 scored, 7 conceded).
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Wales beat Norway 2-1 in Cardiff on 1 Oct 2026 and have won the last three meetings. Overall 12 meetings, four wins each and four draws.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN, refreshed pre-kick-off: Norway 1.25 (-400), draw 6.00, Wales 9.00 (+800), spread -1.5 and total 3.5. The morning read was 1.21 / 6.00 / 10.00 and the opening 1.22 / 5.75 / 8.50. Norway has drifted out slightly and Wales shortened, a small move against the favourite. De-vigged 74.2% / 15.5% / 10.3%. Polymarket live: Norway 0.7765, draw 0.137, Wales 0.0866. Over 24h Norway moved 0.795 to 0.775 (about -2.5% relative). The move is modest and has no news behind it. Polymarket is about 3.5 points above the de-vigged book on Norway, so I shade Norway down to 0.76 and the draw up to 0.15.
checks.models: Unchanged. World Football Elo has Norway 1901 and Wales 1681, a gap of 220 and an expected score of 0.863 for Norway with a draw counted as half. That fits a win probability of about 0.75 to 0.78. Previews from Sports Mole and The Hard Tackle pick Norway 2-1, which is a one-goal win.
checks.venue_weather: Ullevaal Stadion, Oslo, Norway's home ground, grass, kick-off 17:00 UTC. The morning yr.no forecast showed partly cloudy, no rain, light wind, about 5C. No pitch or venue issue reported.

games.reason: Norway are a clear favourite at home. Elo is 1901 against 1681 and the DraftKings de-vigged price is about 74%. The reported XI is strong, with Haaland, Odegaard, Nusa, Bobb and Selvik starting, so there is no heavy rotation. The draw is held at 15%, above Polymarket's 13.7%, because both sides must win, Wales won the last three meetings including 2-1 in October, and Norway have lost three of their last four. Confidence stays medium, not high, because the XIs come from a single unofficial aggregator, I found no official federation or ESPN confirmation, and the price drifted slightly against Norway since the morning (DraftKings 1.21 to 1.25, Polymarket 0.795 to 0.775). No hard exclusion applies.
games.main_risk: Draw or another Wales upset. Wales have won the last three meetings and need a win, Norway have lost three of four group games and conceded in every one, and the Denmark game on 17 Nov is a mild rotation temptation. The XIs are not officially confirmed, Odegaard is one booking from suspension, and the price has drifted slightly against Norway since the morning. A Norway win by one goal (previews pick 2-1) weakens the -1.5 handicap but does not hurt Wales +2.5, which loses only if Norway win by 3 or more.

checks.team_news: Pre-kick-off re-check, about 60 minutes before kick-off. Nothing new found today. No late injury, illness or withdrawal story turned up in a search, and ESPN returned 403 so the summary rosters could not be read. Morning findings still stand. Portugal: Cancelo and Conceicao suspended, Nuno Mendes injured, Leao and Nuno Tavares also reported injured, Palhinha trained Friday after flu-like symptoms. Ronaldo is out (reported retirement, not confirmed by the federation). Denmark: Dorgu out (hamstring), Christensen not called up, Damsgaard status unknown. Costa, Dias, Fernandes and Vitinha: no bad news.
checks.lineups: Official XIs NOT found at the time of this check (FPF/DBU/ESPN summary not reachable; search returned only the 1 October fixture and projections). Still using expected XIs. Portugal (Sports Mole): Costa; Dalot, Dias, Veiga, Nazinho; Vitinha, Fernandes, J Neves; Felix, Ramos, Neto, with Costa in goal. Denmark (Sports Mole): Hermansen; Kristensen, Andersen, Provstgaard, Maehle; Isaksen, Hjulmand, Hojbjerg, Daramy; Hojlund, Froholdt. Unconfirmed, so confidence stays medium.
checks.rotation: Unchanged from the morning. Portugal are already through to the quarter-finals and need a point to win the group; Jorge Jesus spoke of integrating younger players and seven Portugal players are one yellow from a ban, so some changes are possible. No heavy rotation announced and none confirmed (no XI yet). Denmark should be at full strength.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Portugal have little at stake (quarter-final secured, a draw wins the group). Denmark are second on 6 points and need a result, so they are more motivated.
checks.form: Unchanged. Portugal won all 4 group games. Denmark have 2 wins and 2 defeats and scored in all four group games. Hojlund has 3 of Denmark's 7 goals in the competition.
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Portugal beat Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen on 1 October. All-time Portugal 13 wins, Denmark 4, 2 draws in 19. A goal-for-goal draw is the main route to a non-win.
checks.odds: New this evening. DraftKings via ESPN (fetched 18:45 UTC): Portugal 1.56 / draw 4.10 / Denmark 5.00, de-vigged 59.2 / 22.4 / 18.4, opening 1.45 / 4.40 / 5.25, so Portugal have drifted out from the open. Polymarket live 60.7 / 21.7 / 17.7, versus 62.3 / 21.3 / 16.3 this morning. Over 24h Portugal fell from 64.5 to 60.5 (-6.2% relative). That is a continued drift against the favourite, with no team-news story found to explain it. Live leg prices: Portugal draw no bet 82.3, Denmark to score 66.5, Portugal over 1.5 team goals 64.0, BTTS yes 60.5, Over 2.5 62.5.
checks.models: Unchanged. Elo: Portugal 2055, Denmark 1861, expected score for Portugal 0.845. Opta (via Al Jazeera): 59.4 / 21.2 / 19.4. Elo, Opta and the books all point to a Portugal win, but the market is more cautious than Elo.
checks.venue_weather: Estadio Municipal de Braga, Saturday 14 Nov, 19:45 UTC. No weather or pitch problem found (unverified, not treated as a risk).

games.reason: Re-check found no official XI and no new bad news. Portugal remain clear favourites on Elo, Opta and the market. The market drift against them is unexplained (home 64.5 to 60.5 over 24h, 62.3 to 60.7 since the morning), which is why p is set a touch below the morning view. p is within 5 points of the live market on every outcome. Confidence is medium because the lineups are unconfirmed and the price has moved against the favourite. Draw no bet (live 82.3) remains safer than the straight win. Denmark to score is live 66.5; my view is about 67%, since Denmark scored in all four group games and Portugal are missing Cancelo and Mendes.
games.main_risk: A draw (about 21%) or a Denmark win against an already-qualified Portugal that may rotate, with Cancelo, Conceicao and Mendes out. Denmark are more motivated. Lineups unconfirmed and the price is drifting away from Portugal.

checks.team_news: NEW: official XIs are out (ESPN summary, event 401861166). Sweden start Gudmundsson (the thigh/back doubt is cleared), Isak, Gyokeres, Elanga, Nanasi, Ayari, Larsson, Lindelof, Lagerbielke, Svensson and Johansson in goal. Kulusevski is not in the XI, which fits his managed minutes. Bosnia start Zlomislic in goal, Katic, Kolasinac, Radeljic, Dedic, Gigovic, Demirovic, Basic, Alajbegovic, Bajraktarevic and Tabakovic. This is as expected given Muharemovic (suspended) and Hadzikadunic (injured) are out. Jovo Lukic is not in the XI, so his back problem may have kept him out. No new late injury found. The earlier absences still hold: Starfelt, Hien, Holm, Bergvall, Svanberg and Zeneli out for Sweden, and Dzeko retired for Bosnia.
checks.lineups: CONFIRMED per ESPN. Sweden 4-4-2: Johansson; Svensson, Lindelof, Lagerbielke, Gudmundsson; Elanga, Ayari, Larsson, Nanasi; Isak, Gyokeres. Bosnia 3-5-2: Zlomislic; Katic, Kolasinac, Radeljic; Dedic, Gigovic, Demirovic, Basic, Alajbegovic; Bajraktarevic, Tabakovic. Sweden are at full strength up front with the first-choice goalkeeper.
checks.rotation: None. Sweden are at essentially full strength and Bosnia are fielding a settled side. Nothing changed from this morning.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. A Swedish win clinches the group and promotion. Bosnia need a result.
checks.form: Unchanged from this morning. Sweden: W, D 1-1 at Bosnia, W, W, L 0-3 to France. Bosnia are unbeaten in the group.
checks.h2h: Unchanged. The 2 Oct meeting in Zenica ended 1-1, when Bosnia had Dzeko and Muharemovic, and now they have neither.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket: Sweden 0.663, draw 0.203, Bosnia 0.133. The price has not moved against Sweden since this morning (0.660). Over 24h Sweden moved from 0.635 to 0.645. DraftKings via ESPN is now 1.44 / 4.30 / 6.00 (morning 1.40 / 4.40 / 7.00, opening 1.49 / 4.00 / 5.50), de-vigged 63.4 / 21.3 / 15.3, total 2.5. The slight drift back toward Bosnia at DraftKings is small and not tied to any news. Slip legs: Sweden draw no bet is 0.867 at market. Under 3.5 is 0.615 at market, which looks low next to the 2.5 total and the 0.805 for under 4.5. I hold it at the top of the allowed range.
checks.models: World Football Elo: Sweden 1774 v Bosnia 1672, expected score 0.762, about 0.62 to 0.65 win after allowing for draws. That is close to the live market, so the sources agree.
checks.venue_weather: Strawberry Arena, Solna, roof closed, kick-off 19:45 UTC. Not a factor.

games.reason: Official XIs are confirmed: Sweden are at full strength with Isak, Gyokeres and Gudmundsson starting, and Bosnia are missing Muharemovic, Hadzikadunic and Dzeko, so the pre-match view holds. The live price is 0.663 and has not moved against Sweden, DraftKings and the Elo rating agree with it, and no new negative news turned up, so confidence goes from medium to high. I set home 0.65, draw 0.21 and away 0.14, each within 5 points of the market. Leg views: Sweden draw no bet 0.83 (market 0.867), since the 0.65 win and 0.14 loss imply about 0.82. Under 3.5 goals 0.665 (market 0.615). That market price looks too low for a 2.5-total game, but I cap the view at the 5-point limit. The draw remains the main risk to the straight win.
games.main_risk: A draw. Bosnia are compact and unbeaten in the group, and the October game finished 1-1. For the draw no bet leg, the risk is an outright Bosnia win, since Sweden are thin at centre-back. For under 3.5, the risk is an open game: the over 3.5 price is about 38 percent at the market, which is higher than the 2.5 total implies.

checks.team_news: Unchanged from the morning, and nothing new today. Xaver Schlager (right thigh) and Alexander Prass (left thigh) are out, and Marco Grull has also pulled out (Sports Mole). Wimmer, Alaba, Wanner, Chukwuemeka, Wober and Veratschnig are still absent. Ireland report a clean bill of health, with Collins back from his calf problem. No late injury, illness or goalkeeper news found.
checks.lineups: CONFIRMED. The ESPN summary lists the starters for both sides, and bet365 and the Irish Times live blog agree on Ireland. Austria (4-2-3-1): A. Schlager; Posch, Danso, Lienhart, Mwene; Seiwald, Laimer; Lang, Baumgartner, Schmid; Gregoritsch. Danso, Lienhart, Mwene, Posch, Baumgartner, Laimer, Seiwald, Gregoritsch and Schmid all start, so only the known absentees are missing and there is no heavy rotation. Ireland (ESPN lists 3-5-2; bet365 gives a back four): Kelleher; Abankwah, O'Brien or Scales, Collins; Manning, Moylan, Molumby, Azaz; Idah, Parrott. Kelleher is in goal, and an attacking Irish selection (Irish Times).
checks.rotation: No heavy rotation. Austria start their first-choice back four, double pivot and Gregoritsch. Baumgartner may still be limited to about 70 minutes (Rangnick, 13 Nov). Both teams play again Tuesday (Austria at Israel, Ireland v Kosovo).
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Austria lead Group B3 on 8 points, and a win secures promotion to League A. Ireland are on 5 points and need a result.
checks.form: Unchanged. Austria are unbeaten in 14 home games but have no clean sheet in 8 matches. Ireland L,W,D,D in the Nations League.
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Ireland 2-2 Austria in Dublin on 1 Oct 2026 (Ireland led 2-0 at half-time). Draw risk is real.
checks.odds: LIVE now (about 60 min before kick-off): Polymarket home 0.6034 / draw 0.2432 / away 0.1535, versus 0.5966 / 0.2468 / 0.1565 this morning. The price has moved slightly towards Austria and away from Ireland, so it has not moved against the leg. The 24h move on home is flat (0.605 to 0.605). DraftKings (ESPN) is now 1.57 / 3.75 / 5.75, de-vigged 59.1 / 24.8 / 16.1, against an opening of 1.56 / 3.85 / 5.00. Ireland have drifted from 5.00 to 5.75, which is good for the DNB leg. Draw no bet (home_dnb) live 0.8466, which is 1 minus the away price.
checks.models: Unchanged. World Football Elo has Austria 1841 and Ireland 1711, and with home advantage Austria's expected score is 0.79. That fits a 57-60% Austria win and a draw near 25%. Odds and rating sources agree.
checks.venue_weather: Raiffeisen Arena, Linz, kick-off 19:45 UTC (20:45 local). Dry and clear, close to 0C at kick-off. No pitch issue reported.

games.reason: Official XIs are out and confirm the morning picture. Austria are missing only the known absentees (X. Schlager, Prass, Grull and others) and start their strongest available side, with A. Schlager in goal, against an Ireland team that is also at full strength with Kelleher. The price has not moved against Austria; Ireland's price drifted from 5.00 to 5.75 at DraftKings and the Polymarket away price eased from 0.1565 to 0.1535. I keep a small draw shade (25.5% vs 24.3% market) because Austria have no clean sheet in 8 and drew 2-2 in Dublin. For the draw no bet leg, my P(Ireland not winning) is 84.5% against a market 84.66%, essentially fair. The leg loses only on an Ireland win, which needs Austria to lose at home where they are unbeaten in 14. Confidence is high: lineup confirmed, nothing new wrong, price not against the leg, and odds and Elo agree.
games.main_risk: An Ireland win is the only way the DNB leg loses. The risks are Austria's leaky defence (no clean sheet in 8), the early lead Ireland took in Dublin, an in-form Parrott and Idah, and the absence of X. Schlager and Prass. A draw only voids the stake.
